Feeds printmag.com and userresearchstrategist.com failed, five paid Substack posts were removed beforehand.

stories.title: Paul Melcher: surge the derivatives, author the masters, and enforce the line in the tool
stories.blurb: Melcher starts from brand-side marketers complaining that agencies now ship "good enough" work with the wrong logo, and traces it to a choice studios make without announcing it: build around a surge of generated assets, or around authorship. The surge model breaks because approval cost stays human while production cost falls to zero. The authored model breaks because the line between creative and production work is redrawn by vendor roadmaps. His working posture is one master per shoot and layout, derivation automated downstream, and a per-operation rule on whether a generative step may originate content or only adapt it.

sources.name: Design Week
sources.headline: Surge or authorship: which studio are you building?

stories.title: Penguin's design director is in the room early for coffee trucks, a dating night and supper clubs
stories.blurb: Derek Man describes how the publisher reaches lapsed readers (44% of 16 to 24 year olds, per the Reading Agency) by turning up where they are: a Grind coffee van on campuses with an audiobook playlist, a singles event with Thursday Dating, supper clubs next. The design remit starts at positioning the event and extends to the keepsake people take home, which is why he sits with the marketing director and head of brand from the start.

sources.name: Design Week
sources.headline: Derek Man drives the design thinking behind Penguin s events

stories.title: Apple Music's identity was shot in a bath of mineral oil, and the app icon shows none of it
stories.blurb: Creative Boom has the process: Fred Again and NEST Acoustics wrote a short composition, each note was played through a transducer in oil and filmed, and months of tuning were needed because high or dense notes made the surface unreadable. The footage became the note mark, the composition the sonic logo, the wordmark a bold lowercase cut of SF Pro reconstructed by Plau. Creative Bloq points at the gap: the iOS 27.2 icon is black and white and the app only swapped its red accents for blue and yellow, so the part people touch daily carries almost nothing of the brand.

sources.name: Creative Boom
sources.headline: Apple Music s new logo was shaped by Fred Again and a bath of mineral oil

sources.name: Creative Bloq
sources.headline: Apple Music's splashy new logo is gorgeous – so why isn't the new app icon?

stories.title: DixonBaxi turns EA FC's triangle into a free-form shape built to move with culture
stories.blurb: Heinrich Paravicini's brand check on EAFC27: the triangle Uncommon introduced after the FIFA split, a nod to the player cursor, becomes a shape that takes on context-specific interpretations, with a graphic treatment closer to TikTok and Twitch than to TV sports conventions. Creative director Karun Agimal frames it as a system designed to move from campaign to culture rather than a fixed identity.

sources.name: Creative Bloq
sources.headline: The ambitious EA Sports rebrand looks great from every angle

stories.title: East Surrey Council's identity came from six in-house designers, shown anonymously to elected members
stories.blurb: Six designers across the merging councils submitted as many concepts as they wanted, informed by a resident survey, and the team cut them to ten before presenting them without names to councillors, who were steered to set aside personal preference. The chosen mark by Kelly Pink layers leaf shapes for contours and countryside with a hidden lowercase e, set in Lexend. Rollout follows planned renewal cycles rather than replacing assets early, and West Surrey's separately designed brand follows on 10 November.

sources.name: Design Week
sources.headline: East Surrey Council reveals in-house brand identity ahead of 2027 launch

stories.title: Tom Critchlow: whether your brand has an MCP is a boardroom question about ceding the interface
stories.blurb: Critchlow argues the real AI search question is not citation counts but whether a brand helps customers complete tasks inside the model, or becomes an invisible tool call. He lists the split playing out now: Walmart opening an agent gateway while Amazon blocks agents, Notion all in while Figma stays cautious, Booking.com with an MCP and Airbnb without. His position is that every brand should build one, even unreleased, to learn how the interface works, and that its design shapes how agents treat the brand.

sources.name: BRXND Dispatch
sources.headline: Should Your Brand Have an MCP? // BRXND Dispatch vol. 147
sources.author: Tom Critchlow

stories.title: GTA VI trendjacking: Shrek's parody works, Burger King and Axe get called parasites
stories.blurb: Creative Bloq sorts the pre-release wave of Vice City pastiches by legitimacy: other game franchises can play, cars and bikes fit, phone networks and deodorant do not. Much of it leans on AI-generated neon gradients, and the comments under the posts ("who invited him?", "bro, you're not in GTA 6") show audiences reading opportunism faster than brands expect. The point to keep is that a borrowed aesthetic is exhausted within weeks when everyone uses it.

sources.name: Creative Bloq
sources.headline: From Burger King to Shrek, GTA VI trendjacking is going too far

stories.title: State of Brand's 2027 playbook: a brand voice is now copyable from fifty LinkedIn posts, so budget moves to people
stories.blurb: The piece lays out why the old sequence (product, then content volume, then voice) stopped working and where it would put B2B money instead: small events under 200 people with the conversations recorded and published, named customers as sources instead of PDF case studies, and company-run coverage of a trade beat the shrinking press no longer covers. The figures it leans on: 51% of software buyers now start research in a chatbot (G2) and 85% of brand mentions in AI answers come from third-party pages (AirOps).

sources.name: State of Brand
sources.headline: The 2027 B2B Marketing Playbook: How to Get Cited by AI, Seen by Buyers and Shared by Your People | State of Brand

stories.title: Canva Craft plans the layout before it renders, trained on templates rather than photos
stories.blurb: Canva's first own image model works in two stages: a plan with spatial relationships, scale, hierarchy and text, then a render at up to 2K in more than 30 aspect ratios, which the company says is why text stays legible and edits stay local. It was trained on human-made templates from the library, so outputs can be converted into layered designs, and it sits fourth on Design Arena behind three OpenAI models. Available to all users in Dream Lab now, via the API and Canva's MCP later.

sources.headline: Canva’s first AI image model plans designs before generating them
